children: New facility in Karnataka adds 2 lakh units of annual capacity, taking total E-Drive production capacity to 3.6 lakh units

Toyota Kirloskar Auto Parts (TKAP) has invested approximately Rs 460 crore in a new E-Drive manufacturing line at its Bidadi facility in Bengaluru, Karnataka. The line was inaugurated on 16 November and will manufacture next-generation products registered under the Government of India's Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme.

The new facility adds an annual manufacturing capacity of 2 lakh units, taking TKAP's total E-Drive production capacity to 3.6 lakh units per annum. The investment is aimed at strengthening domestic manufacturing of electrified powertrain technologies and supporting the localisation of advanced automotive components.

The inauguration was attended by Dr S Selvakumar, Principal Secretary, Commerce and Industries Department, Government of Karnataka, along with Manasi Tata, Vice Chairperson of Toyota Kirloskar Motor, and Tabrez Ahmed, Managing Director of TKAP.
The new line will operate alongside the company's fourth-generation E-Drive manufacturing line, which was commissioned in 2022.

According to the company, the expanded manufacturing capacity will help reduce dependence on imports and strengthen India's domestic supplier ecosystem for electrified mobility technologies. The E-Drive is a key component of Toyota's hybrid electric vehicle technology.

The project is part of a Rs 4,800 crore memorandum of understanding signed between Toyota Group companies and the Karnataka government to promote advanced manufacturing, localisation, employment generation and green mobility technologies.

Toyota is pursuing a multi-pathway approach to vehicle electrification, which includes hybrid and alternative-energy technologies. The company said its global hybrid vehicle sales have crossed 36.8 million units.
